newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Agrobanka 96 losses seen in billions - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Czech Agrobanka 96 losses seen in billions - c.bank.

text.p: Czech Agrobanka a.s., which suffered through liquidity problems in 1996, lost several billion crowns last year, a senior central bank told a parliamentary banking commission on Friday.

Speaking to reporters after testifying to the commission, central bank Vice-govenror Pavel Kysilka said the figures were preliminary as Agrobanka is still in talks with auditor, Price Waterhouse, on the need for reserves and provisions.
"Information we have talk about several billion (in losses)," Kysilka said.

Price Waterhouse has told Agrobanka it needs to double its reserves to some 10 billion crowns in order to cover potential losses. The bank has said a final audit of the books should be completed in one or two months.

In September, Agrobanka, the fifth largest bank, was placed under temporary forced administration by the central bank because of low liquidity connected to the failure of a smaller Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank is currently searching for a majority shareholder to take control of Agrobanka, which was connected to Kreditni through an secretive investment firm, Motoinvest.
The failure of Kreditni, which investigators said was caused by dubious debt-swap deals linked to Motoinvest, in turn caused a crisis in confidence in Agrobanka.

Agrobanka was the 12th and so far the largest Czech bank to have been subjected to central bank intervention, since post-Communist liberalisation of the sector created dozens of new banks in the early 1990s.

After the wave of collapses, the central bank drew up a plan under which an arm of the state-held Konsolidacni Banka would buy off doubtful assets from small banks at a nominal price for a certain period of time, but the banks would have to adhere to strict rules and close central bank supervision.
Kysilka said on Friday that stabilisation programmes have been approved for three banks -- Banka Hana a.s., Moravia Banka a.s., and Pragobanka a.s..
Three other banks that have entered talks with the central bank are Foresbank a.s., Zemska Banka a.s. .PR, and Universal Banka a.s., he added.
